claims.text: A powder-metallurgy route including controlled hot isostatic pressing will produce a finer-grained high-entropy alloy than conventional casting.
The powder-metallurgy and HIP route will produce more uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates than conventional casting.
The powder-metallurgy and HIP route will improve high-temperature mechanical properties relative to conventional casting.
The conventionally cast baseline has a coarse-grained microstructure.
Powder metallurgy followed by HIP will refine the alloy microstructure.
Reduced grain size contributes to strengthening at elevated temperature.
Uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates provide dispersion strengthening.
Grain refinement and dispersion strengthening enhance elevated-temperature yield strength.
Grain refinement and dispersion strengthening enhance creep resistance at elevated temperature.
At approximately 700°C, the processed alloy will exhibit at least a 15% increase in yield strength relative to the cast baseline.
At approximately 700°C, the processed alloy will exhibit a lower creep rate than the cast baseline.
The predicted improvement applies around 700°C under high-stress conditions representative of extreme environments.
The magnitude of yield-strength and creep-resistance improvement may depend on processing parameters.
